rows.estimation_basis: Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 001-logistics-fleet-portal (Fleet Tracking Portal for a Logistics Operator, 3,400 hours across 20 weeks). In that reference project, multi-vendor telematics integration required 520 hours due to multi-format discrepancies; because this project integrates only a single IoT vendor, telematics ingestion effort is scoped down to 240-300 hours. The live map component (420h in reference) is adapted to 340-420 hours to incorporate server-side clustering lessons learned from the logistics project. The alert engine (380h in reference) is scoped to 280-350 hours for polygon geofence checks and multi-day idle timers. Vehicle CRUD and reporting align closely with the reference modules (scaled to 180-230h and 220-280h respectively). Comprehensive QA, load testing, and stabilization represent roughly 22% of total effort (450-560h), ensuring robust field validation.

No reference projects were provided in the prompt. Estimates were developed bottom-up based on standard enterprise engineering metrics for IoT ingest pipelines, PostGIS geospatial implementations, interactive Mapbox frontends, and production-grade delivery practices (including comprehensive QA, automated testing, DevOps provisioning, and user acceptance testing). Uncertainty regarding the exact protocol and reliability of the single IoT hardware vendor API has been factored into the upper bounds of the integration and testing modules.

Estimates are directly grounded in historical data from Reference Project 'B2B Marketplace for Industrial Parts' (id=003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace, 6,100 total hours). We retained analogous baselines for core marketplace modules: Catalog Import Pipeline (adjusted from 620h to 520-650h focusing on Excel/API rather than legacy XML feeds), Customer-Specific Pricing (adjusted from 780h to 580-720h without complex quote workflows), Stripe Connect Payments (adjusted from 700h to 600-750h), Supplier Portal (adjusted from 820h to 500-640h), and Admin Back-Office (adjusted from 520h to 380-480h). We omitted the 480h Buyer Punch-out (cXML/OCI) module as enterprise procurement integration was not requested. DevOps and QA/UAT hours (380h and 920h in reference) were proportionately calibrated to 320-400h and 700-880h respectively to reflect total scope requirements.

No historical reference projects were provided. Estimates have been derived bottom-up based on standard enterprise engineering parameters for multi-sided B2B marketplace development. The baseline incorporates full delivery lifecycles including requirements refinement, UX engineering, robust QA/E2E test automation, CI/CD infrastructure, security auditing, and post-release stabilization. A contingency buffer is included to absorb uncertainties surrounding supplier file formatting diversity and payment gateway split configurations.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 006 (Embedded Analytics Dashboard for a SaaS Product, 4,600 hours over 24 weeks), which shared near-identical architectural requirements: Kafka event ingestion (520h reference vs 480-560h here), ClickHouse aggregation modeling (640h reference vs 600-700h here), multi-tenant query API (560h reference vs 520-620h here), drag-and-drop dashboard UI (1,000h reference vs 950-1,150h here), scheduled PDF/email reporting (380h reference vs 360-420h here), IaC and monitoring (440h reference vs 400-480h here), performance/stress testing (300h reference vs 280-340h here), and QA/rollout (760h reference vs 700-820h here). Total projected effort ranges between 4,290h and 5,090h, accommodating the lessons learned regarding UX prototyping overhead and strict tenant row isolation testing.

Estimates are grounded directly in historical performance data from reference project 'Internal HR Knowledge Assistant (RAG)' (id=005-hr-internal-ai-assistant, 1,500 total hours across 10 weeks for 400 documents). Given that the current scope encompasses ~600 documents (a 50% increase in policy volume) and carries a mission-critical constraint regarding strict applicant vs. staff data isolation, ingestion and testing efforts have been adjusted upwards. Baseline module hours from the reference (Document ingestion 240h, Retrieval 200h, Chat UI 260h, Access control 180h, Evals 160h, Monitoring 80h, Deployment 140h, QA/UAT 240h) form our minimum baseline (1,500h total), scaled to a conservative upper bound (1,830h total) across 11 calendar weeks to accommodate extensive red-teaming, UAT, and larger corpus validation.

The estimates account for full delivery lifecycle phases including discovery, robust security validation around internal document segregation, automated QA/benchmarking, DevOps provisioning, and stakeholder acceptance testing.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against reference project '002-fintech-kyc-onboarding' (KYC Onboarding Platform for a Digital Bank; 5,200 hours, 26 weeks). The functional scope aligns almost identically across document capture (480h historical vs 440-520h estimated), KYC/sanctions vendor integration (800h historical vs 730-870h estimated), underwriter console with audit trails (720h historical vs 680-760h estimated), rules engine (560h historical vs 520-600h estimated), GDPR encryption (420h historical vs 390-450h estimated), infrastructure & pen-test remediation (640h historical vs 600-680h estimated), and extensive QA/regulatory sign-off support (1,200h historical vs 1,100-1,300h estimated). Total effort is scaled to a realistic delivery window of 26 weeks for a dedicated multi-disciplinary engineering team.

Estimates are directly anchored in historical benchmarks from past production deliveries: Patient Appointment and Telehealth App (id=004-healthcare-patient-app, 3,900h) and Offline-First Field Service App (id=008-mobile-field-service, 3,600h). Specifically, the pet owner mobile application (780-920h) and calendar scheduling engine (480-560h) are mapped directly to 004's patient mobile app (900h) and appointment calendar modules (520h). The notification engine (360-440h) corresponds to 004's messaging and notification module (420h). The clinic staff web console (500-600h) is adapted from 004's doctor web dashboard (560h) and 008's dispatch console (640h). Telehealth video consultation from 004 was omitted as out of scope, while brand-new veterinary-specific modules (in-house EMR, inventory stock management with low-stock warnings, and invoicing) were synthesized using 004's EHR data layer (480h) and 008's ERP parts and invoicing module (520h). QA, store release, and DevOps efforts (580-720h combined) closely mirror historical delivery allocations from both reference baselines.

Estimates are grounded in historical metrics from reference project 008-mobile-field-service (total 3,600 hours over 21 weeks). Specific analogies: Offline Sync Subsystem (680-780h) aligns with the reference offline data layer (760h); Photo Capture and Signature Queue (280-340h) corresponds directly to the reference photo/signature queue (300h); Tablet Inspection Forms (440-520h) reflects the reference checklist engine (520h). The reference ERP integration (520h) and scheduling console (640h) were excluded as outside scope, and replaced by the Safety Incident Register & Multi-tier Approval Workflow (380-480h) and Monthly Site Safety Statistics Dashboard (260-340h). DevOps and QA hours (580-720h total) follow the historical reference allocation (660h total), accounting for thorough offline-condition stress testing and tablet field piloting.

Estimates are grounded in reference project '007-edtech-lms' (total: 2,800h across 18 weeks). We mapped equivalent core modules directly: User Management & SSO (200-240h vs 220h ref), Course Authoring (440-500h vs 480h ref), Video Delivery & Tracking (280-320h vs 300h ref), Assessments & Certificates (340-400h vs 360h ref), and Manager Reporting (260-300h vs 280h ref). We omitted the 420h SCORM package module as it was not required. In its place, we added 560-740h for the custom speaking practice capability (audio capture, speech assessment API pipeline, and feedback UI). DevOps and QA/UAT (420-520h total) are modeled after the reference's 400h allocation, with additional effort included for cross-browser microphone compatibility testing.

DevOps and chat UI requirements remain consistent with the reference architecture.

Estimates are benchmarked against historical data from Reference Project 004 (Patient Appointment and Telehealth App). Specifically, calendar scheduling and conflict management (historical 520h) was adapted to leave clash detection and balance ledger logic (approx. 500h across leave rules and calendar sync modules). Web dashboard workflows (historical 560h) informed the employee and manager approval portals (400-520h total). Security, SSO, and audit logging (historical 300h) provided the baseline for enterprise IdP integration and audit trails (250-330h). Hours have been adjusted downwards from the healthcare reference where specialized clinical integrations (EHR/FHIR) and WebRTC video were not required.

Estimates are grounded in historical metrics from reference project 006-saas-analytics-dashboard (4,600 hours). Specifically, the analytics ingestion, ClickHouse data modeling, and query API components were adapted directly from reference 006 (where ingestion took 520h, ClickHouse modeling took 640h, and query APIs took 560h). We adjusted these estimates downward to 420-540h, 480-620h, and 460-600h respectively, reflecting a specialized, pre-defined metric schema (downloads, country) rather than open-ended custom SaaS event pipelines. The reference's 1,000h drag-and-drop dashboard builder was replaced with a focused 460-600h creator dashboard implementation. Novel functional modules not covered by reference 006 (audio upload processing, RSS syndication engine, embeddable audio player, and multi-tenant podcast RBAC) were estimated bottom-up, factoring in comprehensive end-to-end QA, CDN performance validation, and enterprise DevOps rollout.
